target_customer: Health systems, clinics and commercial genetic testing labs
problem: There are too few genetic counselors for the growing volume of genetic testing. Clear Genetics built software, including a chatbot called Gia, to automate pre-test education, consent and follow-up.
business_model: B2B SaaS to health systems and labs

founders.name: Moran Snir
education: BA and M.Sc. in Biomedical Engineering
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page; later led Software and Data at Invitae after the acquisition.

founders.name: Guy Snir
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page; later COO of Nest Genomics (W22).

founders.name: Motti Shohat
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no further background.

competitors.name: Genome Medical
competitors.what: Telemedicine genetic counseling to address the counselor shortage
competitors.traction_then: Early stage, launching its network in 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: NLP chatbot plus clinical workflow and HIPAA compliant integration with health systems; medically sensitive but not research grade.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical workflows and health system integrations create switching costs, but the chatbot itself was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Invitae, a leading lab, bought Clear Genetics in November 2019 for about 50 million dollars (25M cash, 25M stock per Globes).

market_need_then: A shortage of genetic counselors alongside rapid growth in testing was widely noted in 2017; Geisinger used Gia in its MyCode initiative and Invitae used it in its direct channel before the deal.

branding.domain_note: Used cleargenetics.com, which now redirects to an Invitae page for the Gia chatbot.

identity.mascot_or_character: Gia, the Genetic Information Assistant chatbot

rebrands.why: Folded into Invitae after the acquisition.

brand_strength.rationale: Healthcare press coverage of the Gia chatbot, but a descriptive company name with no community or brand coverage.

outcome_analysis: Clear Genetics tackled a real bottleneck, the shortage of genetic counselors, with a chatbot used by Geisinger and Invitae. After a 2.5 million dollar seed in 2017 it was acquired by Invitae in November 2019 for about 50 million dollars, a strong early exit for a small team. Founders with biomedical and software backgrounds and a testing boom helped.
notes: Seed investors conflict: Seedtable lists Y Combinator, iAngels and Meron Capital; another source says Y Combinator and Compound led; the amount (2.5M) is consistent across sources. CB Insights shows 2.62M over four rounds, so other small rounds may exist, hence partial. Confidence high only for founders and exit; competition rests on one 2017 source. Invitae site fetch was only for the redirect target and the Invitae page was not opened.
